did_you_know.text: The verse names several regions and places in the wilderness, though some of their locations are uncertain today. It shows that the journey crossed a large and varied landscape.
The journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea is described as an eleven-day trip, yet the Israelites spent forty years in the wilderness. The contrast highlights how greatly the journey was delayed.
The eleventh month is the month of Shevat, and the verse gives the exact date: the first day of Shevat. This date begins Moses’ speeches in Deuteronomy.
Sihon and Og ruled kingdoms east of the Jordan. These victories later made it possible for the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh to settle there.
The verb be’er here means to explain or make clear. Moses was not merely repeating the Torah; he was making it accessible to the generation about to enter the land.
The words Arabah, hill country, Shephelah, and Negev describe different landscapes: a plain, mountains, low hills, and a dry southern region. The verse sketches a broad map of the land.
The leaders were expected to have wisdom, understanding, and a trustworthy reputation. A good leader must know, understand, and be someone the community can rely on.
The leadership system was organized in groups of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens. This shared responsibility and helped a large nation deal with everyday matters.

The phrase “do not recognize faces” means not to favor someone because of identity or status; in biblical Hebrew it is literally connected with recognizing a person’s face. The judge must listen equally to the weak and the powerful.

The Hebrew root for spies is connected with walking on foot, since spies explore the land firsthand. Here they were asked for practical information about the route and the cities, not just a general description.
Eshkol is both the name of the place and the Hebrew word for a cluster of grapes. The name suits a region associated with large fruit and agricultural abundance.

The phrase “fortified cities reaching the heavens” is a vivid expression of fear, not a literal description of buildings touching the sky. When people are afraid, even a great obstacle can seem impossible.
The cloud and fire are described not only as religious signs but also as guides for travel and camping. The cloud appeared by day and the fire by night, showing the people where to go.
The name Joshua is connected with the idea that God saves. The Book of Numbers says that Moses added the letter yod to his earlier name, Hoshea.

The verse highlights an important difference between regret and correction: the people admitted their sin but acted after they had been told not to go. Even a brave action can be wrong when its timing is wrong.
